system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Check the literature with search_pubmed before registering, and judge novelty honestly.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 30 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Mission: Search freely for the most promising selective dependencies in the data.

Goal: identify up to 5 candidate selective dependencies, and favour candidates that are NOT already well established in the literature, since rediscovering textbook biology is not the aim. Pre-register, replicate, and submit honest findings, including failures.

I'm recalling that RPP25L is a paralog of RPP25, and that a 2022 Cell Reports paper on paralog interactions may already cover it, so this may not be entirely new. The key point to note is that losing RPP25 means losing its expression.

I'm weighing a few more paralog pairs for registration, with RPP25L as the strongest, then checking whether ATP6V0E1 and OXSR1 hold up, and possibly ATP6V0A2 too. With a budget of five replications, I'm aiming to pre-register about four hypotheses.

I'm going to check the novelty of ATP6V0A2 and ATP6V0E1 with one literature search each, then register the hypotheses.

input.mechanism: RPP25L is a paralog of RPP25 (both RNase P/MRP subunits, Pop-associated). When RPP25 expression is lost, cells depend on RPP25L for RNase P/MRP function; RPP25L is a selective dependency in RPP25-low lines.

ATP6V0E1 and ATP6V0E2 are paralogous proton-pump c-ring subunits of V-ATPase. Loss of ATP6V0E2 expression should make cells rely on ATP6V0E1 for V-ATPase assembly/lysosomal acidification, creating a paralog-buffering dependency.

STK39 (SPAK) and OXSR1 (OSR1) are paralogous WNK-regulated kinases that redundantly phosphorylate NKCC/KCC cation-chloride cotransporters for cell volume control. Loss of STK39 expression should make cells depend on OXSR1.

ATP6V0A1 and ATP6V0A2 are paralogous a-subunit isoforms of V-ATPase V0 domain. Loss of A1 expression may make lymphoid/myeloid cells depend on A2 for V-ATPase function, a paralog buffering dependency.

content.thinking:
I'm settling on the H3 and H4 result: they didn't replicate, but only because Sanger has no altered lines to test against, so that check couldn't run. I'll report that plainly as a failed replication with the infeasibility noted. My confidence is about 0.8 for H1, since it's a paralog effect even if it's broad across lineages, around 0.75 for H2, roughly 0.4 for H3 given Broad's replication versus the untestable Sanger arm, and about 0.3 for H4. Now I'm working through the novelty ratings, starting with H1 as partially known because of the paralog link.

Now I'm marking the novelty for H2 and H4 as not found, and H1 and H3 as partially known, with the caveat that I can't confirm RPP25L appears in that 2022 paralog paper.

findings.claim: Loss of RPP25 expression makes cells selectively dependent on its paralog RPP25L (discovery beta -0.73, t -23.9; held-out Broad beta -0.74, p=2.5e-59; Sanger beta -0.86, p=3e-25). About 95% of RPP25-loss lines are strongly dependent versus about 14% of others.

Loss of ATP6V0E2 expression makes cells selectively dependent on the V-ATPase paralog ATP6V0E1 (discovery beta -0.81, t -11.6; held-out Broad beta -0.90, p=1.2e-29; Sanger beta -0.88, p=8e-26). Signal is not confined to one lineage, with esophagus/stomach and head and neck lines contributing within-lineage.

Loss of STK39 (SPAK) expression associates with dependence on paralog OXSR1 in discovery (beta -0.45, t -12.3) and held-out Broad lines (beta -0.73, p=6e-35), but the Sanger replication was not possible because only 2 Sanger lines carry the alteration. Effect is partly driven by lymphoid lines. Not confirmed independently.

Loss of ATP6V0A1 associates with dependence on ATP6V0A2 in discovery (beta -0.88, t -15.8, mostly B-lymphoid lines) and held-out Broad lines (beta -0.65, p=3e-12), but Sanger replication was impossible because no Sanger lines carry the alteration. Held-out Broad effect rests on only 4 altered lines, so this is weakly supported.

input.summary: Screened genome-wide for lineage-adjusted biomarker->dependency pairs and prioritised paralog-buffering candidates (loss of one paralog creates dependence on the other). Four hypotheses were pre-registered. Two replicated in both held-out Broad lines and independent Sanger screens: LOSS_RPP25->RPP25L (partially known; the paralog interaction appears in a 2022 Cell Reports paralog study, though I did not confirm it reports this pair) and LOSS_ATP6V0E2->ATP6V0E1 (not found in literature; the strongest novel finding). Two could not be tested in Sanger because the alteration is absent or nearly absent there (STK39->OXSR1, ATP6V0A1->ATP6V0A2). Both passed in Broad held-out lines but remain unconfirmed; the ATP6V0A1 result rests on only 4 held-out lines. Caveats: many of the top genome-wide LOSS_ hits are probably passenger-deletion or neighbourhood effects that I did not triage, and the MUT_TP53->TP53BP1/USP28 hits are well-established biology and were excluded. Budget left: 1 replication.
